name: Tinted facial SPF
lead: Tinted facial SPF is a sunscreen for the face with added pigments, often iron oxides, that even out skin tone. Tints come in a range of shades and many products are mineral or hybrid formulas.
It combines daily UV protection and light coverage, which suits minimalist skincare routines.

paras: The UV filters absorb or scatter ultraviolet radiation, and iron oxide pigments also block part of visible light, which can worsen pigmentation conditions such as melasma. A randomized investigator-blinded study in melasma patients found tinted sunscreen reduced the color difference between melasma and normal skin over five months, unlike untinted sunscreen.

Shade range is limited for deeper skin tones and a wrong shade can look ashy or orange. Use enough product: thin application cuts the labeled SPF. Evidence for visible-light protection is mostly from small, sometimes industry-funded trials. The broad sunscreen evidence on skin aging and cancer prevention is strong, and tint adds a cosmetic and pigmentation bonus.

studies.title: Comparison of Visible Light-Protective Tinted Sunscreen to Untinted Sunscreen to Protect Melasma Patients During Summer: A Prospective Randomized Investigator-Blinded Study
